title: Продюсер уже в зале  (The Producer Is Here)

segments.t: Just as the food stylist finishes coating the lamb with varnish and glue for the camera, Dmitry Nagiyev walks into the dining room with his VIP producer because his shoot was canceled early. Let's listen to the Russian scene first.
Дмитрий Владимирович, вы же сегодня на съёмках?
Иди скажи ему, что продюсер уже здесь.
Сказал, что продюсер на месте, можешь подавать блюда.
Now let's go back through their exchange line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Дмитрий Владимирович, вы же сегодня на съёмках?
'Dmitry Vladimirovich, aren't you at a shoot today?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Vika's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
'Thank goodness, it was canceled.' Here Nagiyev anchors the thought on 'glory' and finishes on 'to canceled', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'Is Vitya in his kitchen?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Nagiyev's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
'Yes, he was there.' The past-tense verb ending marks the grammatical gender and number of the subject directly.
Иди скажи ему, что продюсер уже здесь.
'Go tell him that my producer is already here.' Notice how Russian puts 'go, walk' and 'already' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'Let him bring out his cooking.' Here Nagiyev anchors the thought on 'out' and finishes on 'to carry, to bring', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'Enjoy your meal.' In everyday Russian, 'pleasant' flows straight into 'appetite' without extra linking words.
'Stop right there!' Vika delivers this line as an emphatic exclamation, putting strong stress on the main word.
'Now it is filmed. Excellent.' Notice how Russian puts 'now, nowadays' and 'perfectly' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'Thank you. Thank you very much.' Chef Barinov uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.
'Dmitry Vladimirovich has just arrived.' Spoken Russian keeps this brief and expressive, built right around 'arrived' without extra helper words.
Сказал, что продюсер на месте, можешь подавать блюда.

'He said the producer is at his table and you can serve the dishes.' Vika pairs 'said' with 'of dish' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'. Now let's hear the entire conversation once more from start to finish.
Дмитрий Владимирович, вы же сегодня на съёмках?
Иди скажи ему, что продюсер уже здесь.
Сказал, что продюсер на месте, можешь подавать блюда.
That finishes Nagiyev's unexpected early return to the dining room with his film producer. Pay attention to the quick conversational commands and reporting clauses. Until next time!
